questions.question: In Microsoft Word, which option allows you to exclude specific sections or types of text from the spelling and grammar check?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exclusion Dictionary**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Exclusion Dictionary** in Microsoft Word allows you to **exclude specific sections or types of text from the spelling and grammar check**.
 
• It is particularly useful for omitting proper nouns, technical terms, or other specialized language that you don't want to be flagged by the spell checker.
 
• This feature helps maintain the accuracy of the spelling and grammar check by ignoring words that are intentionally spelled differently or are not part of the standard dictionary.
 
• The Exclusion Dictionary can be managed and edited to include or exclude words as needed, providing flexibility in document editing and proofreading.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thesaurus** in Microsoft Word helps **find synonyms and antonyms** for a selected word but does not exclude sections from spelling and grammar checks.
 
• **AutoCorrect** automatically **corrects common spelling and typing errors** as you type, but it also does not exclude specific text sections from checks.
 
• **Spell Check** is the feature that** reviews spelling and grammar** across the entire document, identifying errors but not excluding any sections unless configured through settings like the Exclusion Dictionary.

questions.question: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote a novel Anand Math based on which of the following rebellions/revolts?

__
 
• **Anand Math** is a famous novel written by **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee**.
 
• The novel is based on the **Sanyasi Rebellion**, which took place in the late 18th century against the British rule in India.
 
• The **Sanyasi Rebellion** involved Hindu ascetics (sanyasis) who rebelled against the British East India Company.
 
• The novel is noted for its patriotic themes and the famous song **"Vande Mataram"**, which later became a rallying cry for the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was first published in 1882 and remains a significant work in Indian literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Paika Rebellion** was an armed rebellion against the **British East India Company in 1817 **in Odisha.
 
• The **Kuki Revolt** refers to various uprisings by the **Kuki people** in Northeast India.
 
• The **Mappila Rebellion**, also known as the **Malabar Rebellion**, was an uprising against British authority and Hindu landlords in Kerala by the Mappila Muslims in 1921.
 
• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee is considered one of the greatest writers in Indian literature and his works played a crucial role in the Indian renaissance.

questions.question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following groups of states recorded the lowest literacy rate?
questions.solution:

• The Census of India 2011 is the **15th National census** survey conducted by the Census Organization of India.
 
• **Bihar** had a **literacy rate of 61.80****%**, which was the lowest among all states.
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** had a **literacy rate of 66.95%**, placing it among the lowest literacy rates in the country.

• It is crucial for planning and policy-making processes in various sectors, including education, healthcare, and infrastructure development.
 
• The literacy rate is a key indicator of educational attainment and is defined as the percentage of people aged seven and above who can read and write with understanding.

questions.question: Brihadiswara Temple which exhibits Dravidian temple architecture is located in __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thanjavur**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brihadiswara Temple** is located in **Thanjavur**, Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is one of the largest South Indian temples and an exemplary example of **Dravidian architecture**.
 
• The temple was built by **Raja Raja Chola I** in 1010 AD.
 
• It is a part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known as the "Great Living Chola Temples".
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is also known as **Peruvudaiyar Kovil**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The temple's **Vimana (temple tower)** is one of the tallest of its kind in the world.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **architectural brilliance** and intricate **sculptures**.
 
• The temple complex includes a massive **statue of Nandi (sacred bull)**, carved out of a single stone.
 
• It is an important pilgrimage site and a major tourist attraction in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The Brihadiswara Temple stands as a testament to the **Chola dynasty's** contribution to art, architecture, and culture.

questions.question: The Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022, was enacted to give effect to which of the following?

options.text: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
United Nations Treaty on Oceans relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
United Nations Convention on Oceans and Seas relating to repression of piracy on high seas.
United Nations Regional seas convention relating to repression of piracy on high seas.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea relating to repression of piracy on high seas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022**, was enacted to give effect to the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)** relating to the repression of piracy on the high seas.
 
• UNCLOS provides a comprehensive legal framework governing the rights and responsibilities of nations in their use of the world's oceans, promoting the peaceful use of the seas and the equitable and efficient utilization of their resources.
 
• It includes provisions to combat piracy and armed robbery at sea, ensuring that all states cooperate to the fullest possible extent in the repression of piracy.
 
• The Act enables the Indian government to take stringent measures against piracy, ensuring the safety and security of maritime navigation and protecting the interests of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)** was adopted in **1982 **and came into force in **1994**.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Constitution for the oceans," establishing guidelines for businesses, the environment, and the management of marine natural resources.
 
• UNCLOS has been ratified by over 160 countries, including India, which ratified the convention on** June 29, 1995**.
 
• The convention covers various aspects of maritime law, including territorial waters, contiguous zones, continental shelves, and exclusive economic zones.
 
• India's commitment to UNCLOS is reflected in its national legislation, including the Maritime Anti-Piracy Act, 2022, which aligns with the international standards set by the convention.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers was a part of the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharmapala** was one of the significant rulers involved in the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj.
 
• The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged conflict among three powerful dynasties: the **Gurjara-Pratiharas**, the **Palas**, and the **Rashtrakutas**.
 
• Dharmapala was the ruler of the **Pala Dynasty** and played a crucial role in the contest for Kannauj, a region of strategic importance in Northern India.
 
• During his reign, Dharmapala extended his influence over Northern India and sought to establish his supremacy over Kannauj.
 
• The struggle for Kannauj had significant implications for the control of trade routes and political dominance in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripartite Struggle** lasted for nearly two centuries and was characterized by shifting alliances and frequent battles.
 
• The city of **Kannauj** was highly coveted due to its prime location and economic significance.
 
• Other notable rulers involved in the Tripartite Struggle include **Rashtrakuta King Dhruva** and **Gurjara-Pratihara King Nagabhata II**.
 
• The struggle eventually weakened all three dynasties, paving the way for the rise of new powers in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis Fundamental Duties?

1) They are obligatory in nature

2) Fundamental Rights and Fundamental duties are complementary to each other.

3) The introduction of Article 51A created strong base for a concrete national character and strong harmony.

4) Eleventh fundamental duty was added by 78th constitutional amendment act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eleventh Fundamental Duty was added by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act**, not the 78th.
 
• Fundamental Duties are indeed **obligatory** in nature.
 
• Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties are considered **complementary** to each other.
 
• The introduction of **Article 51A** created a strong base for a concrete national character and strong harmony among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A** was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union and aim to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• Currently, there are **eleven Fundamental Duties** listed in Article 51A of the Constitution.

questions.question: Who among the following is a singer of Hindustani classical music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shubha Mudgal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shubha Mudgal** is a renowned singer of Hindustani classical music.
 
• She has received extensive training in Hindustani classical music from various maestros.
 
• Shubha Mudgal has been awarded several prestigious awards for her contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• Her repertoire includes not only classical music but also Khayal, Thumri, and Dadra styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani classical music** is one of the two principal types of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It has a rich tradition and history and is known for its intricate raga system.
 
• Famous exponents of Hindustani classical music include legends like **Ustad Bismillah Khan, Pandit Ravi Shankar, and Lata Mangeshkar**.
